transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I'm here because I'm just having a hard time staying focused. I get pulled off track pretty easily. Like, if I'm trying to finish a project for school, just a random ping on my phone or... or even just a song lyric or a random thought about something else completely derails me. And then I just kind of lose the thread of what I was supposed to be doing.
Does this difficulty with staying focused happen only when you're working on school projects, or do you notice it in other areas of your life as well, like in social situations or at home?

Um... I guess it happens in other areas, too. Not just school. Like... I've tried doing some small freelance contracts on the side, but I ended up losing them. And I missed out on this portfolio competition recently. Just... people felt like they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly, I guess. 

And with social stuff... some of my friends and collaborators are kind of hesitant to work with me now. They say they like my ideas, but... yeah. It's not just school.
Do you often feel like you are driven by a motor, or do you frequently find yourself interrupting others or acting without thinking?

Um... I guess so. I don't know if I'd call it a motor, but... yeah. Even on days when I don't have classes or a schedule, I don't really just sit there. I end up jumping around... like from editing a prototype to cleaning my desk, or opening a new dataset. Resting just... feels weird, I guess. Like I have to be actively doing something.
When you are in a conversation with someone, do you often find it difficult to wait for your turn to speak, or do you frequently blurt out answers before the other person has finished their question?

Yeah... sometimes. Um. Like when we're brainstorming for a project, I guess I tend to just... blurt my ideas out. Or I'll start adding things to our Figma board before they're even done explaining. I don't really mean to, I just get excited, but... I realize afterward that it probably comes off as kind of pushy. So... yeah.
Looking back at your childhood, say before you were 12 years old, do you remember having these same struggles with focus or impulsivity in school or at home?

Um... yeah, I think so. I mean, my parents used to have to sit right next to me when I did my homework back then. Otherwise, I'd just... wander off, or start doing something else. 

And, um... I guess teachers used to say stuff, too. Like on report cards. Just comments about how I'd rush through worksheets, or... not follow the directions. And they said I talked over people during group work. So... yeah, it's been like this for a while, I guess.

Looking at your current life as an adult, would you say that your struggles with restlessness, impulsivity, and blurting things out are just as prominent and frequent as your difficulties with focus and staying on task?
Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean... they both happen a lot. I don't really know if one is... worse than the other. They just both kind of... happen.

If you look at the last six months, would you say that you have consistently met the criteria for being physically restless or impulsive, or have those specific behaviors become less frequent compared to your struggles with focus?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really kept track of which one happens more lately. They just... both still happen, I guess. I don't know.
